reflections.title: Until Christ Is Formed in You

reflect.text: Before coming to faith, we were trapped in spiritual darkness. Salvation began entirely with God's mercy when He chose to know us and set us free. Yet it is easy to slip back into old habits of trying to earn God's favor through rigid rules, or chasing worldly idols like wealth and ambition. Whatever captures our devotion will eventually shape who we become. Turning back to these human efforts only leads us into slavery all over again.

Trying to secure our standing before God by our own works never brings peace. It only burdens our conscience, because human effort can never satisfy God's holy standard. True Christian freedom means resting completely in grace, which is God's kindness that we do not deserve. Paul longed for the believers to stop relying on outward rituals so that Christ Himself would be formed inside their hearts. Like life slowly growing within an egg, Jesus increases within us as our old selfish habits fade away.

This inner growth often involves deep struggle. Paul compared his care for the church to the pains of childbirth. During times of difficulty and pain, God works to push aside our self-centered desires so that the character of Jesus can be clearly seen in our lives.

questions: Are you trying to earn God's love through your own efforts instead of resting in His grace?
What worldly desires or habits might be hindering Christ from being formed in your daily life?
reflections.prayer: Lord, thank You for knowing me and rescuing me from spiritual darkness. Forgive me when I turn back to selfish ambitions or try to earn Your favor through my own works. Help me to rest in Your grace and allow the character of Christ to grow in me today. Amen.
